text:
zara: ran into a customer bug where hedged upstreams caused duplicate side-effects. they had a payment call behind a streaming generation and the hedged retry hit the payment endpoint twice. oops. we need clear rules for hedging vs side-effects.

jon: yep this has bitten us before. hedging (fan-out to multiple upstream replicas) reduces tail latency but breaks safety if upstream isn't idempotent. we need a policy surface: when to hedge, and how to prevent double-side-effects.

micah: two obvious approaches: 1) forbid hedging on routes marked `side_effects: true` (fail closed) 2) allow hedging but require `Idempotency-Key` semantics at the application layer. both have tradeoffs.

zara: leaning toward a layered approach: default allow hedging for pure-generation routes, but route config must declare `side_effect_policy` with options `forbid|idempotent-only|allow-with-proxy-coordination`. default = `forbid` for anything that touches external systems.

jon: what's `proxy-coordination`?

micah: idea: gateway acts as coordinator for hedged requests with an internal single-flight for side-effecting subrequests. flow: gateway fanouts streaming generate requests to model-pool, but before invoking external payment/email webhooks the gateway ensures only one of the hedged branches actually executes the side-effect via an internal `commit` phase. branches return a `preflight` token which the gateway uses to grant commit to the fastest branch and deny others. requires a small sync hop to commit service.

zara: sync hop might add latency though. For long-running generations it's OK. But for low-latency microflows may be unacceptable. we need a way to prefer no-commit fast path. maybe `commit_strategy: sync|async|none` per route. sync = single-commit gate, async = let one branch commit but de-dupe via idempotency-key on the external system, none = no coordination (hedging forbidden for side-effects).

jon: this also needs a clear request id propagation mechanism. propose `x-rw-request-id` plus `x-rw-hash` per token-chunk when hedging so we can correlate and dedupe logs. Add `x-rw-commit-token` for preflight.

micah: sketch: branch flow:
1) gateway starts two hedged upstreams A/B with same `x-rw-request-id`.
2) model reaches code path that would call webhook, it returns `preflight:{nonce, fingerprint}` to gateway instead of calling external system.
3) gateway decides winner (first preflight) and returns `commit-token` to that branch.
4) winning branch calls external API with `Idempotency-Key: <request-id>` and the `commit-token` header. losing branches abort the side-effect path.

zara: what if preflight never arrives (branch crashed)? gateway should wait up to `commit_window_ms` for preflight then pick whichever arrived or fail-over to different behavior (fallback-only). config knob per route. default `commit_window_ms=150`.

jon: metrics we need: `edge.hedge.attempts`, `edge.hedge.commit_wins`, `edge.hedge.commit_time_ms`, `edge.hedge.dupes_detected`, `edge.hedge.forbidden_blocked` and alert `HEDGE_DUPES > 0` as a hard signal in early rollout.

micah: security/privacy: preflight must not include user data. only include action fingerprint + nonce. external systems must rely on `Idempotency-Key` and be able to return conflict. document our expectations in SDK.

sylvie: SDK teams: we need helpers that abstract this: pipeline wrappers that surface `onPreflight()` and `onCommit()` hooks, plus helpers to surface a unified progress stream to UI when hedging is used (merge fastest tokens). @sdk-bot any comments?

sdk-bot: noted. will add to Node/Python SDK backlog: "Hedged-stream hooks + resume-friendly headers". priority medium.

zara: also consider a simpler hybrid: avoid hedging when route config includes `webhook_endpoints` or `side_effects: true`. most customers doing payments will set that flag. hedging stays enabled for pure text-generation or read-only endpoints.

jon: we should also provide a developer opt-in header `x-rw-allow-hedging: true` for ad-hoc tests, but server-side policy always wins.

micah: tests: create integration harness where we'll spin two model replicas that race; simulate preflight responses, verify only one external call occurs. add chaos tests where preflight delayed beyond `commit_window_ms` and ensure fallback behavior is correct.

zara: billing & tracing: hedged upstreams consume extra compute tokens. record `edge.hedge.compute_ms` and attribute to tenant. also mark trace spans with `hedge.branch=A/B` and a `hedge.winner` tag.

jon: rollout: start with `forbid` default for any routes that declare `side_effects:true`. New flag `edge.hedge.commit-v1` behind feature flag. enable for internal-only customers first.

micah: edge-caveat: for very long-running generative requests, commit coordination might create a head-of-line blocking scenario if many hedges pile up waiting for commits. admission control should limit concurrent hedged side-effecting requests per tenant. add per-tenant quota `max_concurrent_hedges = 10` default.

zara: i'll draft an RFC with: API contract (headers and preflight/commit flow), route config knobs, SDK changes, metrics+billing, test plan, and rollout. will post link here for reviews.

ops-bot: canary deploy: gateway/edge-proxy v1.47.0 -> canary (ap-south-1) scheduled :rocket:

zara: RFC: https://rfc.internal/r/hedged-sideeffect-coordination (WIP) — reviewers: @security @billing @sdk-team.

jon: thanks, this looks like a good start. one last thought: should we allow synthetic commits where gateway can call the external webhook on behalf of branch and return result to winning branch to avoid leaking secrets? might be useful for customers who don't want gateways to orchestrate traffic to their external endpoints. we'll discuss in RFC.

micah: agree add a section: "gateway-mediated commit vs branch-commit" with pros/cons.

zara: thanks all. follow-ups: RFC + test harness + SDK changes. keep rollout behind feature-flag.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded: gateway/edge-proxy v1.47.0 canary -> 1/2 hosts (ap-south-1) succeeded.
